Reference / config/ini

config/ini#

Immutable INI bindings, sections and documents with a bounded text codec.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let settings = IniSection("settings", [IniEntry("name", "Ada")]);
let document = IniDocument(settings);
document.section("settings").value("name"); // "Ada"
document.print(observer); // explicit nominal protocol, no hidden I/O

Description#

Immutable INI bindings, sections and documents with a bounded text codec. The model never infers grammar from a name/value.

Names/values are exact Unicode strings. Empty names, dots, whitespace, case distinctions and normalization variants remain distinct. DEFAULT is an ordinary section, never an ambient parent. Duplicate names are typed errors. Entries replace the old map-shaped API with ordered nominal binding objects.

Section/document constructors snapshot size() once, then item(0..size-1) once in order. Bounds are checked before reading items. Defaults: 1024 entries or 128 sections; an explicit final argument replaces the nonnegative bound. InvalidIniLimit precedes source observation, InvalidIniSize rejects negative size, IniLimitExceeded rejects cardinality above the bound; zero admits empty. Sources are borrowed and never closed. Immutable children remain reachable through the snapshot, while the original sequence is not revisited. Failures from size/item and observers propagate unchanged. No owned resource/destroy.

Duplicate checking sorts the names (O(n log n)); only a document that has a duplicate is scanned again to name the first one. Lookup is O(n). Strings are retained coordinates; container budgets do not limit string length. Parsing and rendering have independent text budgets (docs/std/ini-guide.md). The codec is written in Okkama (#13): no native state, nothing to release.

print() emits each section header followed by entries in order. Empty sections still emit section(name); an empty document emits nothing. Every call repeats the same protocol. Observer errors stop emission. No JSON, reflection or casts.

object ParsedIni#

object ParsedIni does IniContent

Lazy bounded parser. Defaults: 1 Mi Unicode scalars, 128 sections, 10000 total entries; each section <=1024 entries. Negative configuration fails immediately. LF/CRLF, blank lines, whole-line #/; comments, explicit [section], name=value. Bare tokens trim ASCII space/tab. Double quotes support backslash/quote, b/t/n/f/r, uXXXX/UXXXXXXXX scalar escapes. No multiline or inline comments. Raw controls except tab, duplicate decoded names and trailing material fail. Failures carry the one-based line and column, in Unicode scalars, of the first problem in the document. Each value() parses the text again; the result is the same document or the same failure. No file I/O.

object IniString#

object IniString

Lazy canonical text through the nominal print protocol. Each string() starts a new emission; the origin is borrowed, never closed. Every coordinate is double-quoted; ASCII controls are escaped, ordinary Unicode remains literal. Headers/bindings end LF; empty document gives "". Default output bound is 1048576 Unicode scalars; zero permits only empty output. No partial result. A custom emitter must start a section before entries and cannot emit duplicate names. Even if it catches an observer exception, string() repeats that failure.
